newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS sees 1997 oil output at 34.3 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS sees 1997 oil output at 34.3 mln T.

text.p: Russia's second-largest oil company YUKOS plans to produce 34.3 million tonnes (686,000 barrels per day) of crude oil in 1997, up from 33.6 million tonnes (672,000 bpd) in 1996, YUKOS said in a statement Monday.
It also said it plans to boost sales this year by 740 billion roubles from the 1996 total of 23.62 trillion roubles.
The production total did not include YUKOS' share of joint venture production, a press spokesman said.
YUKOS is one of around a dozen vertically-integrated oil companies created over the last few years in Russia, and its main production unit is Yuganskneftegaz.
YUKOS said in December last year that it expected oil production to fall in 1997 to 32.6 million tonnes (652,000 bpd).

The spokesman said that YUKOS planned to export 2.0 million tonnes (40,000 bpd) more oil in 1997 than the 8.5 million (170,000 bpd) it exported last year, the bulk of the increase going to the former Soviet republic of Belarus.
The company planned to refine 21.7 million tonnes (434,000 bpd) of oil in 1997, up from 18.3 million (366,000 bpd) in 1996.
YUKOS said 19.4 million tonnes (388,000 bpd) of the total would be its own crude in 1997 from around 14.4 million (288,000 bpd) in 1996.
